precepts.text: For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves. Baruch clears up the word bethink easily. In the land of our captivity, the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves.
precepts.point: Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness. Bethink means to remember. What is Solomon saying here in prayer? Solomon saw in the spirit us being put on ships and scattered all over the world, yokes being put upon our necks, and then being destroyed afterwards so much that we would turn our own eyes against our own people and attack them. That is why he said they must bethink or remember themselves, because Solomon saw in the spirit that we were going to lose ourselves, lose our identity, and try to seek others or recreate ourselves, and not recreate ourselves in the image of God. And we can only say, we have sinned, if we know who we are.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

precepts.why:
Solomon prays, “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”. Bethink is not a common word we use today. Baruch clears it up easily: “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.”

“For I knew that they would not hear me”: that is why he put us in captivity, because we are a stiffnecked people. He delivered us to the enemy, by ships, “unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. This land is the land of our enemy: our enemy conquered us and made this land his land. Far is here, far from Jerusalem; near is Africa or Madagascar, colonised just the same.

“but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” In our captivity, in the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves. That is what bethink means: remember, call to mind. Solomon saw in the spirit our people put on the ships and scattered all over the world, yokes put upon our necks, and destroyed so much that we would turn our own eyes against our own people and attack them. He saw that we would lose ourselves and our identity, and try to seek others or recreate ourselves, instead of in the image of God.

So first we must remember ourselves. We can only say “We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness” if we know who we are. And once you learn who you are, you learn who the enemy is by default. As long as you don’t know who you are, you will make your own people from the continent or the Caribbean your enemy, while the white man gets a pass.

precepts.text: That they might bring up the ark of the covenant out of the city of David, which is Zion. Y'all see that? So Jerusalem was also called Zion.
precepts.point: The Lord God hath sworn by himself, I abhor the excellency of Jacob: because all 12 tribes was going off. Therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein. So the southern kingdom was going to get it, and the northern kingdom.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria”. At ease in Zion: that is the southern kingdom. Trust in the mountain of Samaria: that is the northern kingdom. How do we know Zion is Judah’s Jerusalem?

“Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.” The city of David, which is Zion. So Jerusalem was also called Zion.

So Amos is speaking a woe to both houses at once: Judah at ease in Zion, and the northern kingdom trusting in Samaria. And he tells them both what is coming: “I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces: therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein.” All twelve tribes were going off, so the southern kingdom was going to get it, and the northern kingdom too.

precepts.text: Blessed be the Lord that hath given rest unto his people Israel according to all that he promised; there hath not failed one word of all his good promise which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.
precepts.point: His mouth commanded it and his spirit gathered them; he cast the lot for them and divided it unto them by line, as the land was divided: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and David got big portions, Obadiah, Micah, Amos, Jonah, and Nahum small ones. They shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation: we will possess the land for ever and the word of God for ever.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail”. We must all get into the habit of consistently reading, four chapters a day minimum, because not one prophecy in it shall fail. Solomon witnessed it at the dedication of the temple:

“Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

Not one word failed of what he promised by Moses, and not one word shall fail of what he promised by Isaiah. The same God who gave Israel rest in the land according to all that he promised has promised the day of the Lord’s vengeance, “the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion”, the sword coming down upon Idumea and the great slaughter in the land of Edom. We are living the controversy of Zion now, with Amalek claiming the land is theirs.

None of the promises in this Bible shall fail. That is why we seek out of the book of the Lord and read: what he said by his prophets will come to pass just as surely as the rest he gave Israel in the days of Solomon.

precepts.text: If they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent.
precepts.point: This is not a time of peace but of war; not physical war, but uniting, keeping the law and waiting on the Redeemer.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel shall be “as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”: dispersed, so that we could be preserved. And “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” We are hearing that now and seeing it now. Our teachers tell us these things, we identify with them, and that is how we regain our identity.

Solomon’s prayer shows the steps: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

First we have to bethink ourselves: remember ourselves and reclaim our identity, right here in the land of our captivity. That is part of the strangeness of our salvation. Then we repent and make supplication, and then God will acknowledge us, be for us and fight for us.

This is not a time of peace but a time of war. Not physical war: there is nothing we can do against these powers and nations physically. What we can do is unite as a people, come back together, keep God’s laws in solidarity, and wait on our Redeemer. In the place where we were called not his people, we remember who we are, we repent, and we are called the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: A perfect heart is one that walks in His statutes and keeps His commandments; that is the meaning of be thou perfect.
precepts.point: Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
What does “be thou perfect” mean? The scriptures define it: “Let your heart therefore be perfect with the Lord our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.” A perfect heart is one that walks in His statutes and keeps His commandments. That is how Israel perfects itself.

Abram was ninety and nine years old when he was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse. And Christ said nothing new in Matthew 5:48; the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before, right here to Abram, and it has always meant keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: Give them compassion before them who carried them captives; the Lord gave Joseph that compassion in Egypt.
precepts.point: The Most High deals with His people even in captivity and gives them compassion before them who carried them captive; the favor on Joseph is the pattern of that prayer.

note.label: Genesis 39: Joseph in Potiphar's House

precepts.why:
“And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them.” That is the prayer for Israel in captivity, and the favor on Joseph is the pattern of it.

Joseph was carried captive, brought down to Egypt and bought by Potiphar out of the hands of the Ishmeelites. Yet “the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master “saw that the Lord was with him”, Joseph “found grace in his sight”, and Potiphar made him overseer over his house and put all that he had into his hand. The Lord gave Joseph compassion before the man who held him.

The Most High deals with His people even in captivity. He blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake, “and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.”

precepts.text: If they bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent; the remembering begins in the captivity.
precepts.point: Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

note.label: Exodus 20: The Ten Commandments

precepts.why:
“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

To bethink is to remember. The remembering begins in the captivity, in the land of them that carried them captives. Remember the Sabbath day is a word to a people who forgot it there and must bethink themselves and repent.

precepts.text: If they bethink themselves in the land of their captivity, and repent, and return unto thee with all their heart, the Most High hears; repentance in captivity brings the covenant back to remembrance.
precepts.point: The land enjoys her sabbaths while she lieth desolate without them, and the people must accept that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
When the people repent and turn back, the Most High remembers His covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, the covenant passed down to their children, the children of Israel, and He remembers the land. Solomon prayed for exactly that at the dedication of the house.

“If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near; Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

That confession is what accepting the punishment of their iniquity looks like: the people owning that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes. “And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land”: repentance in captivity brings the covenant back to remembrance, and the Most High hears.

precepts.text: Solomon said the exact same thing: blessed be the Lord that hath given rest unto his people Israel; there hath not failed one word of all his good promise which he promised by the hand of Moses.
precepts.point: There failed not ought of any good thing which the Lord had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass. Everything the Most High said he would do and every good thing he promised, he did it, because God does not lie.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

precepts.why:
“There failed not ought of any good thing which the Lord had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.” Solomon said the exact same thing: “Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

Rest according to all he promised, and not one word failed. In Joshua's day the Lord gave them rest round about and delivered all their enemies into their hand; in Solomon's day it was still true. Everything the Most High said he would do and every good thing he promised, he did it, because God does not lie.

precepts.text: In those days ten men out of all languages of the nations shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you, the same joining of the nations to the house of Jacob that Solomon foresaw.
precepts.point: He prays that when Israel goes out to battle against the enemy in the way the Lord sends them and prays toward the city and the house, the Lord hear their prayer and maintain their cause. So the Most High hears the stranger's prayer out of respect for Israel, but he does not hear a prayer aimed against his people.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

That is the same joining of the nations to the house of Jacob that Solomon foresaw when he prayed for the stranger “that is not of thy people Israel, but cometh out of a far country for thy name’s sake”, that “all people of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee, as do thy people Israel”.

The nations come because they have heard that God is with Israel. That hearing of the nations comes only when Israel is right and in rulership, not while Israel is in captivity and sin. The Most High hears the stranger’s prayer out of respect for Israel; he does not hear a prayer aimed against his people. When Israel goes out to battle where he sends them, he will “hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.”

precepts.text: Solomon and all Israel kept the feast seven days and seven days, even fourteen days, the earlier pattern Hezekiah's congregation repeated.
precepts.point: There is great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon there had not been the like, and the priests and Levites bless the people and their prayer reaches heaven, his holy dwelling place.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

precepts.why:
“And at that time Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God, seven days and seven days, even fourteen days.” That is the earlier pattern Hezekiah’s congregation repeated.

They “kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness”, and then “the whole assembly took counsel to keep other seven days: and they kept other seven days with gladness.” Fourteen days in all, all in one mind and one heart. Hezekiah gave “a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep”, the princes “a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep”, and all the congregation, the priests, the Levites and “the strangers that came out of the land of Israel” rejoiced together.

So it fits that “there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was not the like in Jerusalem.” The priests and Levites blessed the people, “and their prayer came up to his holy dwelling place, even unto heaven.”

precepts.text: There is no man that sinneth not; when the captives in the land of their enemy repent, confess they have sinned and done perversely, and turn again with all their heart, God hears their prayer.
precepts.point: When we recognize we are in our transgressions and iniquity and we repent, then the Lord hears us.

note.label: Job 33: Elihu Speaks God's Instruction to Man

precepts.why:
Elihu says if any man says, “I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not”, God “will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.” Solomon prayed the same thing: “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness; And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul”, then “hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause”.

There is no man that sinneth not. When the captives in the land of their enemy repent, confess they have sinned and done perversely, and turn again with all their heart, God hears their prayer. When we recognize we are in our transgressions and iniquity and we repent, then the Lord hears us.

precepts.text: In captivity, repent and make supplication saying we have sinned and committed wickedness; then He hears the prayer and maintains our cause. He only hears when we repent.
precepts.point: To make supplication is to plead, ask forgiveness, and confess specifically what we have done. You cannot just say "Lord I have sinned"; you must name what you are dealing with.

note.label: Psalm 30: Joy Cometh in the Morning

precepts.why:
“I cried to thee, O Lord; and unto the Lord I made supplication.” To make supplication is to plead, ask forgiveness, and confess specifically what we have done. Solomon shows how it is done in captivity: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

You cannot just say "Lord I have sinned"; you must name what you are dealing with: we have sinned, done perversely, committed wickedness. “And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers”.

“Then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause”. When we repent and make supplication in captivity, He hears the prayer and maintains our cause. He only hears when we repent; that is why He hid His face and David was troubled, and why David cried and made supplication.

precepts.text: There is no man that sinneth not; when Israel sins the Most High delivers them into the hand of the enemy, carried away captive.
precepts.point: The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
Solomon prayed, “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. There is no man that sinneth not, and when Israel sins, the Most High delivers them into the hand of the enemy, carried away captive.

That is exactly what happened to us. A lot of people do not think we deserved to come over here on slave ships, or deserve to be shot down in the streets, or deserve the curses put on us. But we sinned against the Most High. The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. David says “I acknowledge my transgressions”, and that is what we must do.

precepts.text: When Israel is smitten before the enemy because they have sinned, they must turn again and confess his name.
precepts.point: The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house”. Israel is smitten before the enemy because they have sinned. The way back is to turn again to the Most High and confess his name.

That is what David does in Psalm 51: “I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.” Acknowledging the sin is the first step of turning again. We were smitten down before the enemy because we sinned against the Most High, and we have to confess it the same way.

precepts.text: In the land of captivity we must bethink ourselves and repent, saying we have sinned and done perversely and committed wickedness.
precepts.point: The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”. In the land of our captivity we must bethink ourselves and repent, saying we have sinned, and have done perversely, and have committed wickedness.

That is David's “I acknowledge my transgressions” said as a nation. We are in the land of them that carried us captive, and there is no man that sinneth not. Instead of saying we did not deserve it, we bethink ourselves, acknowledge that we sinned against the Most High, and make supplication to him from here.

precepts.text: We cry daily to the Lord keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ until He hear us.
precepts.point: His eye mourneth by reason of affliction; he has called daily upon the Most High and stretched out his hands unto Him. When the Lord turns His face from us, a lot of this stuff is relevant to us today, like the dead bodies laying in the streets of the great city.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
The psalmist is “shut up” and “cannot come forth”, afflicted with all the Lord's waves, yet he says, “I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.” Solomon prayed for exactly this for Israel in captivity: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

That is the supplication of Psalm 88 from the lowest pit. In the land of them that carried us captive we bethink ourselves, repent and say we have sinned. So we cry daily to the Lord, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, until he hear us.

precepts.text: Zion is Israel.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, His righteousness. When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.”

Zion is the city of David, and the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes are gathered to it. Zion is Israel. So when Isaiah says Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, the redeemed of the Lord in the psalm are the Israelites.

precepts.text: Solomon assembled the elders of Israel to bring up the ark out of the city of David, which is Zion; Zion is another word for Jerusalem or Israel.
precepts.point: Zion is another word for Jerusalem or Israel. Jerusalem or Israel was a people before it was a place, so when scripture refers to Zion it points to the children of Israel.

note.label: Psalm 149: The High Praises and a Two-Edged Sword

precepts.why:
“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.” Solomon assembled the elders of Israel to bring up the ark of the covenant “out of the city of David, which is Zion.” Zion is another word for Jerusalem or Israel. Jerusalem or Israel was a people before it was a place, so when scripture refers to Zion it points to the children of Israel.

The King the children of Zion are joyful in is the same horn of his people, the horn of salvation, which is Christ. He will beautify the meek with salvation; meek means submissive or obedient, so if you keep the commandments and are obedient to the Most High you will have salvation. Then come the high praises in the mouth and a twoedged sword in the hand: the honour the saints, the children of Israel, receive when they overcome these people is the privilege of binding their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron. If you do not understand that we are Israelites, you will read this and think it is talking about a time during David or during the kings, but it is talking about the future.

precepts.text: We would have to acknowledge our offenses before the Most High, and in the affliction of the other nations we return to Him.
precepts.point: The houses thrown down by the mount and the sword would be filled with the dead bodies of men He slew in His anger, for He hid His face from the city for all their wickedness.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
Solomon prayed for the very affliction Jeremiah is watching come: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

We would have to acknowledge our offenses before the Most High. He hid his face from the city for all their wickedness, and it is in the land of them that carried us captive, in the affliction of the other nations, that we bethink ourselves, repent, and return to him. Then the one who hid his face answers when we call.

precepts.text: When Israel is smitten because they sinned, if they turn again and confess and make supplication, the Most High will hear and forgive.
precepts.point: The one speaking told Daniel that from the first day he set his heart to understand and to chasten himself before the Most High, his words were heard, and he came for his words. The Most High heard Daniel's supplications and prayer because he was beloved, and gave him these visions for the same reason. It is the same with Israel, the beloved of the Most High.

note.label: Daniel 10: A Man Clothed in Linen

precepts.why:
From the first day Daniel set his heart to understand and to chasten himself before the Most High, his words were heard. That is Solomon's prayer being answered: “When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house: Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest unto their fathers.”

Israel was smitten because they sinned, and Daniel turned again, confessed and made supplication. The Most High heard Daniel's supplications and prayer because he was beloved, a man greatly beloved, and gave him these visions of what shall befall his people in the latter days for the same reason. It is the same with Israel, the beloved of the Most High: when Israel turns again, confesses and makes supplication, he will hear and forgive.

precepts.text: If they bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and say, We have sinned, and return unto thee with all their heart in the land of their enemies, and pray toward their land.
precepts.point: The deliverance comes by knowing who you are. There is a doctrine to it: acknowledge the fault, repent, and make supplication, and do it in the land of the enemy where you are.

note.label: Zechariah 2: The Measuring Line and the Apple of His Eye

precepts.why:
Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. This is a future prophecy as well as a past one; the scriptures are twofold. And there is a doctrine to how Zion delivers herself. “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness; And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies”. Acknowledge the fault, repent and make supplication, and do it in the land of the enemy where you are, praying toward the land he gave to our fathers.

The deliverance comes by knowing who you are: spread abroad as the four winds of the heaven, in the land of the enemy, and told to bethink ourselves there.

precepts.text: Let your heart therefore be perfect with the Lord our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments.
precepts.point: Everything from verse 38 down is charity, and charity is the bond of perfectness.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
“Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” Solomon shows what a perfect heart is: “Let your heart therefore be perfect with the Lord our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.”

Perfection here is a heart perfect with the Most High, walking in his statutes and keeping his commandments. That is how a man is perfect as his Father in heaven is perfect.

precepts.text: Zion is the city of David, which is Israel, so believing "in Zion" is believing in Israel.
precepts.point: The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes “that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.”

Zion is the city of David, which is Israel. So the stone laid in Zion is laid in Israel, and believing in Zion is believing in Israel. The whosoever that receives remission of sins through his name is whosoever of Israel.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
Still dealing with liberty to the captives. “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them,” And God was angry with us. “and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near;” Delivered us to who? To the enemy. Where? Unto the land of the enemy, like the United States of America.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;” So King Solomon was prophesying that the Israelites would be carried away captive, and if we wanted deliverance from captivity we would have to bethink ourselves: remember who we are as a people, remember that we are the twelve tribes of Israel. We would also have to repent and make great supplication to the Lord and confess with our mouth, we have sinned, we have done perversely, we have committed wickedness. We're in that process now, each and every one of us.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
No one of these shall fail: Solomon explains it. “Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised:” Here it comes. “there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

Many times people ask how do you know the Bible is a true book, it's been published and republished and translated and retranslated over and over again. Simple. The way you know the Bible is truth is Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. Did we go into slavery on ships? You better believe that thing right there did not fail. Did we have yokes of iron on our necks? Not one word of that thing failed. Were our sons and daughters taken from us and given to another people? That word did not fail. Did we become proverbs and byword wherever we scattered? That word didn't fail. Were we removed into all kingdoms and nations of the earth? That word surely did not fail. So we know the Bible is true based on that alone. We might forget the promises, because we're in the curses right now, so we're going to use them curses to our advantage and reveal that them curses only fit our people, and not one word that God said through Moses has failed.

And if somebody can't see Deuteronomy 28, leave them alone. They got to be dumb as a rock. If you can't see that we went into slavery on ships historically, you're an idiot, a walking talking idiot, and I'm wasting my time talking to you. The only way you can disprove the Bible is to prove that slavery never happened to our people. That's the only way.

This gathering is a feast of dedication for the temple, not the later feast of dedication remembered in Maccabees, but a first feasting to dedicate the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: The priests and Levites bring up the ark, the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels, while Solomon and all the congregation sacrifice sheep and oxen that could not be numbered for multitude.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: The priests bring the ark into the oracle, the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubims, whose wings spread over the place of the ark and covered it and the staves. The staves, the handles for carrying the ark, are drawn out so their ends are seen in the holy place before the oracle but not seen without, and there they remain.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: There is nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone that Moses put there at Horeb, when the Lord made the covenant with Israel as they came out of Egypt.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: When the priests come out of the holy place, the cloud fills the house of the Lord so that they cannot stand to minister, for the glory of the Lord filled the house. Solomon says the Lord said he would dwell in the thick darkness, and that he has built a house for the Most High to abide in forever.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: Solomon turns his face about and blesses all the congregation of Israel, standing before them, a black king addressing the whole nation of his people. He blesses the Lord God of Israel who spoke with his mouth to David and fulfilled it with his hand.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: He recounts that since the day the Most High brought Israel out of Egypt he chose no city to build a house, but chose David, and though it was in David's heart to build the house, the Lord said his son would build it. That word is now fulfilled, Solomon risen up in David's room, sitting on the throne, having built the house and set a place for the ark of the covenant.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: Solomon stands before the altar in the presence of all the congregation and spreads forth his hands toward heaven, praying that there is no God like the Lord in heaven above or earth beneath, who keeps covenant and mercy with those who walk before him. He asks the Most High to keep the promise to David that his seed shall not fail a man on the throne, if his children take heed to walk before him.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: Solomon confesses that the heaven of heavens cannot contain the Most High, how much less this house, yet he asks that the Lord's eyes be open toward this house night and day, and that he hearken to the prayers made toward this place and forgive. This teaches us to face our homeland and pray, and to build a prayer life like our forefathers.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: Solomon lays out the causes for which Israel would pray toward this house: when a man trespasses and swears before the altar, that the Lord judge between the wicked and the righteous; when Israel is smitten before the enemy for sin and turns again and confesses, that the Lord forgive and bring them back; when heaven is shut up and there is no rain because of sin, that he forgive and give rain.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: The weather itself, the rain and the drought, is bound to whether Israel is in sin or not, for the whole world and the sun, moon, and stars were made for the children of Israel. Solomon adds that when any plague of a man's own heart drives him to spread his hands toward this house, the Lord who alone knows the hearts of men will hear, forgive, and give to every man according to his ways.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: Solomon prays that even a stranger of a far country who hears of the great name and strong hand of the Most High and comes to pray toward this house be heard, that all people of the earth may know the name of the Lord and fear him as Israel does. This hearing of the nations comes only when Israel is right and in rulership, not while Israel is in captivity and sin.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: He prays that when Israel goes out to battle against the enemy in the way the Lord sends them and prays toward the city and the house, the Lord hear their prayer and maintain their cause. So the Most High hears the stranger's prayer out of respect for Israel, but he does not hear a prayer aimed against his people.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: Solomon prays for the day Israel sins and is carried captive to the land of the enemy, far or near, that if they bethink themselves, repent, and turn again with all their heart, confessing plainly the wickedness they have done, the Lord hear their prayer, maintain their cause, and forgive. He asks that the Most High give them compassion before those who carried them captive.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: No other nation on the earth has this way out, that when it sins it can always turn to the Most High, face the east, and pray for forgiveness, because he separated Israel from among all people of the earth to be his inheritance, brought forth out of the furnace of iron of Egypt. The luxuries Israel is afforded even in captivity are because the Lord is on their side.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: When Solomon finishes praying he rises from kneeling with his hands spread to heaven and blesses all the congregation with a loud voice, blessing the Lord who has given rest to his people, not one word failing of all his good promise by the hand of Moses. He asks that the Lord be with them as with their fathers, incline their hearts to keep his commandments, statutes, and judgments.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: He asks that his words of supplication be near the Lord day and night, that the Most High maintain the cause of his people at all times, that all the people of the earth may know the Lord is God and there is none else. Therefore let the heart be perfect with the Lord, to walk in his statutes and keep his commandments.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: The king and all Israel offer sacrifices before the Lord, Solomon offering a peace offering of twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep, so the king and all the people dedicate the house of the Lord. He hallows the middle of the court to offer there because the brazen altar was too little to receive the multitude of offerings.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

points: Solomon holds a feast, and all Israel with him from the entering in of Hamath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord seven days and seven days, even fourteen days. On the eighth day he sends the people away, and they bless the king and go to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness the Lord had done for David and for Israel his people.
